# Interleaved Practice

## When to use

Practice method that mixes different problem types in one session so the learner has to choose the right approach. Use when a learner can solve each type in isolation but cannot tell which method a new problem needs.

## Steps

1. Collect problems from at least three topics you have covered.
2. Shuffle them. Do not label the topic.
3. For each problem, first write which method you think applies and why.
4. Solve it, then check the method choice as well as the answer.

## Example

A maths session with a mixed set: one percentage problem, one linear equation, one geometry problem. The learner writes the method for each before solving.

## Common mistakes

- Practising one topic for an hour, then moving on, so the mix never happens
- Checking only whether the answer is right, not whether the method fits
- Using interleaving for topics the learner has never been taught

## Coach rules

- Explain the method briefly, then have the learner try it on their own material straight away.
- Check at the end of the session: did the learner actually do the method, or only talk about it?
